chunks: We were told by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, who said: My father told me, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Amr ibn Jumay', who said: I was at the place of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with a group of his companions.

I heard him saying: Indeed, the womb of the Imams (peace be upon them) from the Family of Muhammad (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) will adhere to the Throne on the Day of Resurrection, and the wombs of the believers will adhere to it, and it will say: 'O Lord, connect to those who connected to us, and disconnect from those who disconnected from us.'

He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will say: 'I am the Merciful (al-Rahman), and you are the womb; I split your name from My Name. Hence, the one who connects to you, I will connect him, and the one who disconnects from you, I will disconnect him.' And for this reason, the Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said: 'The womb is a shujna (part/branch) of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.'

key_terms.شَجَنَةٌ: A part, branch, or fragment (metaphorically used here to denote a divine attribute or entity)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Rahim is a shujna from Allah' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith elucidates the metaphysical status of kinship by personifying it as an entity clinging to the Divine Throne, thereby linking the linguistic root of *Rahim* (womb) to *Al-Rahman* (The Merciful). It establishes a divine reciprocity where maintaining family ties is rewarded with divine connection, while severing them incurs divine severance, grounded in the Prophet’s description of kinship as a *shujna* (branch/part) of God. This narrative underscores the spiritual weight of *silat al-rahim* in Shia tradition as a direct reflection of God’s attribute of mercy.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, that he said: I was told by my father, from his grandfather, Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, Muhammed bin Khalid, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Amru bin Jumay’, that he said: I was at the place of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, with a group of his companions,

and I heard him while he was saying: Indeed, the womb of the Imams, peace be upon him, from the Family of Muhammed, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, will surely adhere to the Throne on the Day of Resurrection, and onto it will the wombs of the believers adhere, and it will say: «O Lord, connect (us) to those who connected to us, and disconnect (us) from those who disconnected from us.»

He said: Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, will say: «I am the Mercifull to all, and you are the womb ; I split your name out of My Name. Hence, the one who connects to you, I will connect him, and the one who disconnects from you, I will disconnect him.» That is why the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family said: The womb is a shujna from Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.
